sections.html:
Dorchester sits on the Mid-Eastern Shore of Maryland. Cambridge is its seat and biggest city. The 2020 census counted 32,531 people, and the 2025 estimate is 33,628. Cambridge had 13,096 residents, and 13.9 percent of its 6,464 housing units were empty.

With about 33,600 residents countywide, buyers come from a small local pool, and many properties are rural parcels, waterfront lots or older town houses. Water covers 442 of the county's 983 square miles, which shapes both pricing and insurance.

About 55 percent of the land in Dorchester County sits in the 1 percent annual chance floodplain, and nearly 75 percent is below 20 feet in elevation. Those figures come from the county's 2022 Flood Mitigation Plan update.

  • A 1% flood would affect 2,440 buildings countywide, with about $37.1 million in estimated losses.
  • In the City of Cambridge, 126 buildings would be affected, about $2.65 million in losses.
  • The county has 54 repetitive loss properties in the unincorporated areas and Cambridge, plus 3 severe repetitive loss properties.
  • Hurricane Isabel in 2003 pushed storm surge over 8 feet in some areas, and Tropical Storm Isaias in 2020 brought a federal major disaster declaration.

Church Creek, Eldorado and Galestown lie fully within storm surge zones. If your house is near the water, buyers will ask about elevation, flood insurance and past claims. Gather elevation certificates, insurance declarations and any claim history before listing so the buyer's lender has less to stall on.

July is when bills are mailed. A full annual bill, or the first half of a split one, is due September 30, and the second half is due December 31. One county office collects real property tax for every municipality inside the county.

Payment options are the online Tax and Utility Bill portal, the mail, or the County Office Building at 501 Court Lane in Cambridge. The county main number is 410-228-1700, and the Department of Finance answers at 410-228-4343. The office closes for Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Day and Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

After the due dates, unpaid accounts gain interest and a penalty, and the lien can move toward the county's tax sale. Interest runs monthly, so ask Finance for a payoff figure on the exact day you plan to close.

sections.h2: Tax rates in Dorchester County and Cambridge
sections.html:
Unincorporated Dorchester County had a real property rate of 1.0000 per $100 in fiscal 2025, and the county rate in the newer state table is 1.0300 for fiscal 2026. Towns add a rate of their own.

Area (fiscal 2025)County rateTown rateTotal per $100
Unincorporated Dorchester County1.0000none1.0000
Cambridge0.92670.80961.7363
Hurlock0.91790.72031.6382

A Cambridge house carries a far higher combined rate than a similar one in the open county. If you own both a town house and a rural parcel, compare the two bills before deciding which to list first.

Transfer and recordation tax

State tables list a county transfer tax of 0.75 percent and a recordation tax figure of $5.00. The title company works out the real charge from the deed and the price, and prints it on the settlement statement.

The county runs its tax sale online. In 2025 bidding opened at noon on June 16 and closed at noon on June 17, so expect a mid-June window and confirm the date with the finance office each year.

  • The 2025 sale covered unpaid taxes and fees for tax years 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025.
  • Bidders registered online for a $50 fee.
  • Paying in full by 4:00 p.m. on June 12, 2025 pulled a property out of the sale.
  • Owners also owe a $50 advertising fee per property, plus interest as the law provides.

State rules let you redeem until a court forecloses. Foreclosure can be requested six months after the sale, nine for an owner-occupied home, and a certificate with no case filed in two years becomes void.

An owner in Dorchester climbs the same three-rung appeal ladder as everyone else in Maryland, and the first rung closes 45 days after the notice date. SDAT revalues property roughly every third year and mails each owner a Notice of Assessment.

  1. Start with the Supervisor of Assessments and file within 45 days of the notice date.
  2. Next comes the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, which needs your request within 30 days.
  3. Last is the Maryland Tax Court, 30 days after the board issues its order.

Between reassessments, you can file a petition for review no later than the first working day after January 1. Someone who buys after January 1 and before July 1 gets 60 days from the transfer date, once the deed is on record. If you are selling in that window, tell your buyer the option exists. It costs nothing to raise and can lower their bill later.

An unpaid tax bill does not block a sale. Settle the balance ahead of the cutoff and the house drops off the list. Miss it, and the lien can still be paid out of your proceeds at closing, only with extra fees and interest in the total.

  1. Call the finance office and ask for the total through your closing date.
  2. Ask whether the town also bills separately, which matters in Cambridge and Hurlock.
  3. Hand the payoff to the title company so it lands on the settlement statement.
  4. Keep the paid receipt in case the buyer's lender asks.

Timing around the sale list

The tax sale covers accounts that are still unpaid in the spring and early summer, so the best time to clear a balance is before then, when only interest is running. After advertising begins, the $50 advertising fee per property is added. Waiting until the last day leaves no room for a bank wire to clear or a check to be posted, so give yourself a few days of cushion before the cutoff. If a buyer is financing, the lender will want proof that the tax is current before it funds, and an unpaid balance will delay that approval.

Cash buyers tend to close sooner than financed ones, useful when a sale date looms. A flood-prone or older house also tends to run into lender appraisal issues that a cash purchase avoids.

faqs.q: When are Dorchester County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The annual bill and first installment are due September 30, and the second installment is due December 31. Interest and a penalty start once those dates pass.

faqs.q: How much of Dorchester County is in a floodplain?
faqs.a: About 55 percent of the county's land lies in the 1 percent annual chance floodplain, and nearly 75 percent is under 20 feet in elevation.

faqs.q: What is the property tax rate in Cambridge?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2025 total is 1.7363 per $100, made of a 0.9267 county rate and a 0.8096 town rate. Unincorporated Dorchester County totals 1.0000, so check the current year before you rely on these numbers.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Dorchester County house before the tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the tax and fees before the cutoff and the house leaves the sale list, or let closing pay the balance from proceeds. In 2025 the payment deadline was June 12 at 4:00 p.m., so ask the finance office for the current date.

faqs.q: What is the Dorchester County transfer tax?
faqs.a: State tables show 0.75 percent for fiscal 2025 and 2026. Who pays, and any exemptions, depend on the contract and the deed, so confirm with the title company.
